concerns.text: The primary outcome `review_effort_duration` for LLM‑generated PRs is *synthetically simulated* (Section 1.1) by sampling from a KDE built on human PRs conditioned on the same five covariates that are later used for propensity‑score matching. This makes the validation target (synthetic review time) a deterministic function of the predictors, creating a circular/tautological validation: the metric being tested is constructed from the very variables used to control for confounding, so any statistical test will at best reflect the simulation procedure rather than real reviewer effort. Consequently the analysis cannot answer the research question “do LLM‑generated code require longer review time?” and violates independence of outcome from predictors.
